paper_sections.title: Longitudinal changes in rsFC following CBT

description.value: Resting-state functional connectivity of rostral anterior cingulate, anterior subcallosal cingulate, and Brodmann area 25 seeds was examined in patients with major depressive disorder before and after cognitive behavioral therapy, including baseline symptom-severity associations, longitudinal connectivity changes, and prediction of treatment outcome.

spans.text: In the current study, using resting state fMRI (rsfMRI) data from the same set of subjects, we used the rACC, and two subregions of the SCC (BA25 and aSCC) as seeds and examined (a) correlates of depression symptom severity in MDD at baseline; (b) correlations between longitudinal changes in rsFC and clinical improvement; and (c) prediction of treatment outcome with CBT using baseline rsFC.

description.value: Interventional longitudinal study of unmedicated patients with current major depressive disorder receiving 14 sessions of cognitive behavioral therapy, with healthy volunteers scanned at baseline and follow-up without intervention.

spans.text: Resting-state data were collected from unmedicated patients with current MDD (Hamilton Depression Rating Scale-17 > 16) before and after 14-sessions of CBT monotherapy.
Fifty-three participants (20 HVs and 33 patients with MDD) enrolled and completed baseline rsfMRI.
14 45-min sessions of CBT for depression were administered over approximately 12 weeks according to a treatment manual [ 26 ].
